    The canonical representation carried by a string word #

    The basis vectors of a string representation are the occurrences of vertices along the word. We represent an occurrence by the prefix ending there. This retains repeated visits to the same displayed vertex without choosing numeric coordinates.

    A displayed arrow acts between two prefix occurrences when the word traverses that arrow positively between them, or traverses its formal inverse in the opposite direction. Reduction makes the resulting target occurrence unique.
